govdocs-archive_org-nsia-DoleRobertSenat: Howard Kurtz’s Washington Post piece — Behind the Scenes: Media Reporting of the Dole Affair — covers press coverage of Bob Dole. Kurtz covered the media beat. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-KautenMarieMat_: Harold Weisberg’s letter to Mr. and Mrs. Kauten — January 22, 1977 — is a researcher’s note. Weisberg answered his readers kindly. The letter may hold a clue. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-ODanielPat_ODan: This Dallas Times Herald item — JFK Probe Requested, Pat O’Daniel, 1968 — is a press file. Calls for a new probe never stopped. The call was heeded. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
betty-gordon-in-washington-or-strange-ad: Alice Emerson sends Betty Gordon to Washington, D.C., where strange adventures await among the capital's monuments and mysteries. Betty's pluck and good sense see her through in this lively series installment. A fun tour of the nation's capital wrapped in a girls' mystery.
the-gold-bat: Wodehouse's school story revolves around the Gold Bat — a cricket trophy — and the boys of Wrykyn who play for it. Mischief, sport, and schoolboy honor fill this early tale from the master-to-be. A must for Wodehouse fans and lovers of the classic school story.
the-swoop-or-how-clarence-saved-england-: Wodehouse's wildest flight of fancy: nine nations invade England at once, and only Clarence the Boy Scout can save the day. Written in a fortnight, it is pure comic anarchy. The master's silliest — and most lovable — book. Nine powers invade at once in this madcap tale, and only a quick-witted boy scout stands between England and ruin.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alfred-the-gr: This 1913 reference piece on Alfred the Great — England's beloved king and scholar. Thomas Taaffe honors his heroic life. He beat the Danes and taught his people. His translations lit the dark age. The only English king called Great. His statue stands in Winchester's square.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anne-madelein: A 1913 entry on Anne-Madeleine Remuzat — the Visitandine of the Sacred Heart. Joseph Dedieu-Barthe honors her visions. Marseilles heard her message. Her cause moves toward the altars. A nun of the Heart's devotion. Her writings spread the Heart's devotion.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antoine-and-g: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on the Duprats — Antoine, chancellor and cardinal of France, and Guillaume his kin. Joseph Sollier tells their story. The Concordat of Bologna was Antoine's work. He ruled church and state for Francis I. The mighty chancellor of the Renaissance.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arnaud-d-ossa: A 1913 entry on Arnaud d'Ossat — the cardinal diplomat of Henry IV's absolution. Antoine Dégert honors his statecraft. His letters are models of the art. Rome prized its Gascon servant. The prince of the papal diplomats. His red hat crowned long service.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aurora-lucis-: This 1913 reference article on Aurora lucis rutilat — the Easter dawn hymn. Joseph Otten unfolds its joyful verse. The light's dawn reddens the sky. The Office sings it at Lauds. The hymn of the risen morning. Its melody is ancient and joyful.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ballarat: This 1913 reference piece on Ballarat — the Australian diocese of the goldfields. Henry Cleary gives its roaring story. The diggers built its churches. The Eureka stockade tested its peace. A bishopric of the Victorian gold. Its archbishop rules the western district.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-barlaam-and-j: This 1913 reference article on Barlaam and Josaphat — the Buddha tale made Christian. Francis Mershman traces its wondrous journey. The Indian prince found the faith. The legend charmed medieval Europe. The most famous religious romance. Their feast graces the calendars. Their story crossed half the world.
